aldersgate-church-lubbock-tx-gmc.assessment: Aldersgate Church in Lubbock was founded in 1985 when a preacher began knocking on doors inviting people to a new church experience — the first service was held August 4, 1985 in the gymnasium of All Saints Episcopal School. The congregation voted 97% to disaffiliate from the UMC and has joined the Global Methodist Church. Lead Pastor Ryan Smallwood (married to Amy, two adult sons Blake and Jeb) leads with a conversational teaching style. Notable: Emily Fisher serves as Next Gen Pastor, meaning women do serve in pastoral roles at this particular local church — a YELLOW flag on the gender rubric for readers committed to strictly male-only pastoral offices. The lopsided disaffiliation vote signals strong institutional orthodox commitment, however. Named for John Wesley's famous May 1738 Aldersgate Street conversion experience.

all-saints-anglican-charlottesville.assessment: All Saints Anglican is a standout conservative Anglican congregation in Ivy, just west of Charlottesville. Father Sean McDermott leads a parish rooted in the Anglican Province of America — a body that explicitly departed from the theologically liberal Episcopal Church (TEC) to maintain orthodox Christianity. The parish is notably associated with Ken Myers, founder of Mars Hill Audio Journal, as choir director — giving it an unusual depth of cultural and theological engagement. The APA ordains men only, holds to the 39 Articles, and maintains the historic Book of Common Prayer tradition. For a man drawn to liturgical worship, ancient prayer traditions, and sound orthodox theology, All Saints is exceptional. Note: APA is distinct from both TEC (liberal) and ACNA (the other Anglican break).

all-saints-church-crec-new-holland-pa.assessment: All Saints Church in New Holland, PA (Lancaster County) was established in 1999 as a church plant of Christ Church (Moscow, ID) and is a member of the CREC. Dr. Gregg Strawbridge served faithfully as pastor for twenty years (2002–2022) and is the founder of the Strawbridge Ministerial Forum hosted by the church. Following his passing in 2022, Rev. Kasey Horvath (lead) and Rev. Brandon Gilanyi (associate) were installed in 2023, and the congregation relocated to a historic building in New Holland in 2024. Theologically this is a classic Moscow-network CREC congregation: Reformed, covenant-renewal liturgical worship, paedocommunion, classical Christian education ethos, patriarchal household vision, and postmillennial cultural engagement. The one area calling for direct inquiry is soteriology — CREC churches have historically been associated with Federal Vision theology, which modifies traditional Reformed articulations of justification. Ask the elders directly about their position on FV and justification. For a Reformed man in Lancaster County seeking a serious, liturgical, Moscow-aligned CREC home, this is the obvious first visit.

score_notes.christology: Orthodox Trinitarian, Nicene Christology. CREC affirms historic creeds.
score_notes.scripture: High view of Scripture — Reformed, confessional, affirms inerrancy in the classical Reformed sense.
score_notes.gender: CREC is explicitly patriarchal — Doug Wilson's network has led the Reformed critique of 'soft complementarianism.' Male-only elders and pastors. Household-centered, anti-feminist.
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of male pastors/elders (Horvath + Gilanyi, installed 2023). CREC polity with denominational accountability.

all-saints-opc-suffolk-va.assessment: All Saints Orthodox Presbyterian Church is a congregation of the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), the confessional Reformed denomination founded in 1936 by J. Gresham Machen. OPC churches subscribe to the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms, restrict ordained office to qualified men, and practice presbyterian polity with accountability through session, presbytery, and General Assembly. Baseline green rating reflects confessional identity; verify local particulars on the website.

score_notes.gender: OPC Book of Church Order restricts the offices of teaching elder, ruling elder, and deacon to qualified men only (1 Tim 2–3; Titus 1).
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of ordained male elders (session) under presbyterian polity with accountability to the presbytery and General Assembly.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed soteriology per Westminster — monergistic regeneration, sola fide, sola gratia, sola Scriptura, effectual calling, perseverance of the saints.
score_notes.cultural: OPC historically resists theological accommodation to cultural pressure — Machen's legacy of confessional fidelity over cultural relevance.
score_notes.denominational: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — founded 1936 by J. Gresham Machen as a confessionally Reformed denomination against Modernism in the PCUSA.
score_notes.preaching: OPC pulpits are characterized by expository, Christ-centered, Law/Gospel preaching from the Westminster tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: OPC congregations typically emphasize family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church — strong formation pipeline for men.
score_notes.mission: OPC Committee on Foreign Missions and Home Missions actively plants confessionally Reformed churches domestically and abroad.

all-souls-anglican-atlanta-ga-acna.assessment: All Souls Anglican Church is an ACNA parish in the Anglican Diocese of the South, serving Atlanta with a Sunday 4:15 PM service at 1950 Bolton Road (northwest Atlanta). Rector Rev. Collin Setterberg leads the congregation, which self-describes as 'a deeply-rooted, grace-filled Anglican parish' with three core values: pursuing beauty in Christ, practicing presence through weekly communion and prayer, and participating in spiritual restoration.
